facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration of 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
On 8 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 8 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered that the applicant be placed in pre-trial detention until 8 August 2012.
On 15 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 15 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m. on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square, unidentified persons called those present to move outside the agreed meeting venue and to defy the lawful orders of the police.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the unidentified persons' calls led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.

The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Articles 212 § 2 and 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment.

The applicant's sentence of three years and six months' imprisonment was calculated on the basis of a three-year prison term under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, partly concurrent with a term of one year and four months under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
